arxiv-2109-05620.title: in Proc. of EMNLP 2021 (short) RockNER: A Simple Method to Create Adversarial Examples for Evaluating the Robustness of Named Entity Recognition Models
arxiv-2109-05620.creator: Bill Yuchen Lin, Wenyang Gao, Jun Yan, Ryan Moreno, Xiang Ren
arxiv-2109-05620.description: Abstract To audit the robustness of named entity recognition (NER) models, we propose RockNER, a simple yet effective method to create natural adversarial examples. Specifically, at the entity level, we replace target entities with other entities of the same semantic class in Wikidata; at the context level, we use pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) to generate word substitutions.

arxiv-2312-12385.title: Input Compression with Positional Consistency for Efficient Training and Inference of Transformer Neural Networks
arxiv-2312-12385.creator: Amrit Nagarajan, Anand Raghunathan
arxiv-2312-12385.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Amrit Nagarajan, Anand Raghunathan. Transformers have rapidly increased in popularity in recent years, achieving state-of-the-art performance in processing text, images, audio and video. However, Transformers present large computational requirements for both training and inference, and are prone to overfitting during training. To address these challenges, we present Input Compression with Positional Consistency ( ICPC ), a new data augmentation method that, unlike prior augmentation techniques, simultaneously improves both generalization and training efficiency.

arxiv-2404-15863.creator: Fabio Deelan Cunden, Marilena Ligabò, Maria Caterina Susca
arxiv-2404-15863.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Fabio Deelan Cunden, Marilena Ligabò, Maria Caterina Susca. For quantum observables H H truncated on the range of orthogonal projections Π N \Pi_{N} of rank N N , we study the corresponding Weyl symbol in the phase space in the semiclassical limit of vanishing Planck constant ℏ → 0 \hbar\to 0 and large quantum number N → ∞ N\to\infty , with ℏ ​ N \hbar N fixed.

arxiv-2408-09035.title: Multi Teacher Privileged Knowledge Distillation for Multimodal Expression Recognition
arxiv-2408-09035.creator: Muhammad Haseeb Aslam, Marco Pedersoli, Alessandro Lameiras Koerich, and Eric Granger
arxiv-2408-09035.description: Abstract Human emotion is a complex phenomenon conveyed and perceived through facial expressions, vocal tones, body language, and physiological signals. Multimodal emotion recognition systems can perform well because they can learn complementary and redundant semantic information from diverse sensors. In real-world scenarios, only a subset of the modalities employed for training may be available at test time.

arxiv-2506-24118.title: Scaling human judgment in Community Notes with LLMs
arxiv-2506-24118.creator: Haiwen Li, Soham De, Manon Revel, Andreas Haupt, Brad Miller, Keith Coleman, Jay Baxter, Martin Saveski, Michiel A. Bakker
arxiv-2506-24118.description: Abstract This paper argues for a new paradigm for Community Notes in the LLM era: an open ecosystem where both humans and LLMs can write notes, and the decision of which notes are helpful enough to show remains in the hands of humans.

arxiv-2509-19658.title: RoboSSM: Scalable In-context Imitation Learning via State-Space Models
arxiv-2509-19658.creator: Youngju Yoo, Jiaheng Hu, Yifeng Zhu, Bo Liu, Qiang Liu, Roberto Martín-Martín, Peter Stone
arxiv-2509-19658.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Youngju Yoo, Jiaheng Hu, Yifeng Zhu, Bo Liu, Qiang Liu, Roberto Martín-Martín, Peter Stone. In-context imitation learning (ICIL) enables robots to learn tasks from prompts consisting of just a handful of demonstrations. By eliminating the need for parameter updates at deployment time, this paradigm supports few-shot adaptation to novel tasks. However, recent ICIL methods rely on Transformers, which have computational limitations and tend to underperform when handling longer prompts than those seen during training.

On the entry of the French into Naples and the establishment of the Parthenopean republic (1799) he adhered to the new government, and when the Bourbon king Ferdinand IV. pmc-10670460.creator: Chengxia Sun, Lijun Geng, Xian Liu, Qing Gao, Matteo Convertino

pmc-11306276.creator: Andreas Karlsson Rosenblad, Bassam Mazin Hashim, Per Lindblad, Börje Ljungberg, the National Swedish Kidney Cancer Register Steering Committee
pmc-11306276.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). PurposeTo examine associations between ablative therapy (AT) and partial nephrectomy (PN) and the occurrence of local recurrence (LR), distant metastatic recurrence (DMR) and all-cause mortality in a nation-wide real-world population-based cohort of patients with nonmetastatic renal cell carcinoma (nmRCC).MethodsData on 2751 AT- or PN-treated nmRCC tumours diagnosed during 2005–2018, representing 2701 unique patients, were obtained from the National Swedish Kidney Cancer Register.

pmc-11433765.title: Preoperative Factors on Loss of Range of Motion after Posterior Cervical Foraminotomy
pmc-11433765.creator: Dong-Ho Lee, Hyung Rae Lee, Sang Yun Seok, Ji Uk Choi, Jae Min Park, Jae-Hyuk Yang
pmc-11433765.description: Background and Objectives: Posterior cervical foraminotomy (PCF) aims to resolve cervical radiculopathy while preserving range of motion (ROM). However, its effectiveness in maintaining ROM is uncertain. This study investigates the changes in ROM after PCF and identifies preoperative factors that influence ROM reduction post surgery.

pmc-11643830.title: Investigation of the Influence of Fused Deposition Modeling 3D Printing Process Parameters on Tensile Properties of Polylactic Acid Parts Using the Taguchi Method
pmc-11643830.creator: Getu Koro Megersa, Wojciech Sitek, Agnieszka J Nowak, Neven Tomašić, Rubén Paz
pmc-11643830.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Despite Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) being an economical 3D printing method known for its material versatility and ease of use, the mechanical performance of FDM-produced components is significantly influenced by process parameter settings. This study investigated the effects of the layer thickness, raster angle, build orientation, and extrusion temperature on the ultimate tensile strength (UTS) and elastic modulus of Polylactic Acid (PLA) specimens using Taguchi methods, with significance analyzed through analysis of variance (ANOVA).
